title: 第一章 渗透政治：朝鲜移民与日本帝国
originalTitle: Chapter One · The Politics of Osmosis: Korean Migration and the Japanese Empire

zh: 日本把占领朝鲜视为殖民满洲、中国本部、印度乃至最终殖民亚洲其余地区的第一步。在这样的梦里，日本帝国的扩张并不取决于宗主国与各殖民地之间的依附关系——即后者作为资源供给者或市场服务于前者。相反，这个梦建立在殖民者与被殖民者之间错综复杂的关系之上：后者充当一系列容器，让日本的主权力量顺着这些容器逐级向外渗透，形成一个广大的亚洲共同体。我把这种层层递进的帝国构建策略概念化为渗透政治。在渗透过程中，体现日本在满洲权力的，是朝鲜人移动的身体，而非静止的制度或可移动的物品本身——就像一个不断扩张的更大身体的细胞网络。这种权力主张被动员为一种策略，用以排挤中国对朝鲜人及其土地的管辖权，确立对满洲的宗主权。渗透政治既蕴含领土扩张的逻辑，也蕴含资本主义扩张的逻辑；下文对安寿吉（An Sugil）小说《北间岛》（Pukkando）的阅读，正是这一政治的寓言。与小说阅读相关的问题包括：日本当权者与朝鲜农民作为同床者、都梦想获得土地的关系；朝鲜人作为殖民者与被殖民者的双重位置；以及民族主义时间与资本主义时间所组织起来的社会，即朝鲜人、中国人和日本人展开三角关系的场域。
en: Japan considered the occupation of Korea to be the first step in the colonization of Manchuria, China proper, India, and ultimately the rest of Asia. In such a dream, the expansion of the Japanese empire hinged not on a dependent relationship between the metropole and each colony, with the latter serving the former as a provider of resources or a market. Rather, the dream rested on an intricate relationship between the colonizer and the colonized, with the latter acting as a series of vessels that would allow Japan’s sovereign power to flow outward in succession, from one to the next, forming an extensive Asian community. I conceptualize this cascading strategy of empire building as the politics of osmosis. In the osmotic process, the moving bodies of Koreans, not immobile institutions or movable things per se, embodied Japan’s power in Manchuria like the cellular webs of a larger, expanding body. This claim to power was mobilized as a strategy to displace Chinese authority over Koreans and their lands and establish suzerainty over Manchuria. The politics of osmosis entailed the logic of territorial expansion and the logic of capitalist expansion, for which a following reading of Pukkando, a novel by An Sugil, works as an allegory. Issues pertinent to the reading of the novel include the relationship between the Japanese power holders and Korean peasants as bedfellows who both dream of obtaining land; the dual position of Koreans as colonizers and colonized; and the social as a locus of the triangular relations among Koreans, Chinese, and Japanese that is organized by nationalist and capitalist time.

zh: 阅读《北间岛》
en: reading pukkando

zh: 满洲在朝鲜文学想象中占据了新的位置：殖民时期，朝鲜作家定居间岛（满洲吉林省的一个地区，即今延边朝鲜族自治州），即使在朝鲜本土禁用朝鲜语之后，仍用朝鲜语写作。被殖民者在新边疆的生活激发了满洲想象的创作。朝鲜人的困境、他们在土匪与中国地主手中遭受的苦难，以及新的肥沃土地的诱惑，都是关于满洲的常见文学表象。由于这些作家中许多人在解放后前往北朝鲜生活，冷战期间韩国读者基本读不到他们的作品。

解放后移居韩国的最知名作家之一是安寿吉，他曾供职于满洲的朝鲜语报纸《满鲜日报》（Mansŏn Ilbo）。在安寿吉的重要作品中，《北间岛》与更具争议的《北乡谱》（Pukhyangbo）形成对照。后者于1944至1945年在《满鲜日报》连载，把朝鲜人描绘为忠诚的殖民臣民，把日本官方为迁居的朝鲜农民开辟农场的计划当作自身事业。《北乡谱》让作者背负了与殖民者合作的名声，《北间岛》则可算作一部救赎之作。《北间岛》1959至1967年间写于韩国，两卷本叙述了1860年代至1945年朝鲜人移民满洲的史诗，以及夹在中国民族主义与日本帝国主义之间的生活。第二卷处理1910年代初至1945年的时期，是一部正统民族主义叙事，把朝鲜人描绘为帝国主义的受害者与反日斗争的英雄。但第一卷——我阅读的重点——对更早的时期提供了罕见的记述，这一时期在民族主义文学与满洲历史研究中大多被忽视。更重要的是，对朝鲜人早期定居时期的表象，为理解朝鲜人的双重主体性提供了关键洞见：他们作为满洲的殖民者经营生活，而自身又被日本殖民。
en: Manchuria occupied a new place in the Korean literary imaginary, since Korean writers settled in Kando (a district of Jilin Province in Manchuria and currently the Korean Yanbian Autonomous Prefecture) during the colonial period and wrote in Korean even after its use was banned in Korea. The lives of the colonized on a new frontier galvanized the production of Manchurian imaginaries. The plight of Koreans, their suffering at the hands of bandits and Chinese landlords, and the allure of new, fertile land were familiar literary representations of Manchuria. As many of these writers went to live in North Korea after liberation, their works were largely unavailable to South Korean readers during the cold war.

One of the best-known writers who moved to South Korea after liberation is An Sugil, who worked for Mansŏn Ilbo, a Korean newspaper in Manchuria. Among An’s key works, Pukkando stands in opposition to Pukhyangbo, which is more controversial. Published as a serialized novel from 1944 to 1945 in Mansŏn Ilbo, the latter portrays Koreans as dedicated colonial subjects who embraced as their own Japan’s official project of creating new farms for relocated Korean peasants. While Pukhyangbo branded the author as a collaborator, Pukkando can be counted as a work of redemption. Written between 1959 and 1967 in South Korea, Pukkando’s two volumes narrate the epic of Korean migration to Manchuria from the 1860s to 1945 and lives caught between Chinese nationalism and Japanese imperialism. The second volume, which treats the period from the early 1910s until 1945, is an orthodox nationalist narrative that depicts Koreans as victims of imperialism and heroes of anti-Japanese struggle. But the first volume, the focus of my reading, offers a rare account of the preceding period, which has been largely overlooked in nationalist literature and historical studies of Manchuria. More importantly, the representation of the earlier period of Korean settlement offers essential insights into the dual subjectivity of Koreans, who negotiated their lives as colonizers of Manchuria who were themselves colonized by Japan.

zh: 《北间岛》属于这样一种民族主义文学：它把农民设想为新历史的主体，在这段新历史中，农民不仅保住生计，还成为现代民族的开明成员。小说中，农民的社会生活与现代公民的社会生活形成辩证对立——无能的政府无法保护贫困农民免受自然灾害，迫使他们迁往新边疆。家庭的代际团结化解了这一对立，导向生产性的农耕与更强大的民族。主人公家族的谱系始于从朝鲜南部迁往与中国接壤的地区。这次迁移是官方守卫朝鲜领土工程的一部分：1432年朝鲜王朝从中国取得北部图们江一带后，为守住领土而组织移民。家族与邻人的第二次背井离乡发生在四百年繁荣之后：持续的干旱使家族陷入财务崩溃。这与法国、俄国、美国、日本军舰来袭之后的新民族危机同时发生。19世纪末，这个家族迁往间岛北部——北间岛（Pukkando）。
en: Pukkando belongs to a nationalist literature that envisages peasants as the subjects of a new history in which peasants not only secure their means of living but also become enlightened constituents of a modern nation. In the novel, the social life of peasants is dialectically opposed to that of modern citizens, as the inept government cannot protect impoverished peasants from natural calamities, forcing them to relocate on a new frontier. The generational unity of the family resolves this opposition, which leads to productive farming and a stronger nation. The genealogy of the protagonist family begins with its migration from southern Korea to a region bordering China. This migration is part of an official project of guarding Korean territory after the Choson state obtained the northern Tuman River region from China in 1432. The second uprooting of the family and its neighbors comes after four centuries of prosperity, when a persistent drought results in the family’s financial devastation. This coincides with a new national crisis following the attacks by French, Russian, American, and Japanese warships. In the late nineteenth century, the family moves to (northern) Kando—Pukkando.

zh: 迁往间岛北部代表着家族与民族的生存。一方面，从字面上说，这是贫苦农民最后的求生尝试：当迁移被禁止、违者处死时，农民的选择是饿死还是被国家处决。另一方面，迁往间岛在比喻意义上是通往新朝鲜民族的通道。《北间岛》的主人公之一Hanbok，是少数冒死在间岛耕种的朝鲜人之一。间岛与Hanbok在朝鲜的村庄仅隔一条图们江，在那里耕种需要每天渡江。他通常摸黑出发去间岛，通宵耕作后在黎明前回家。Hanbok的秘密耕作被儿子无意暴露——男孩用三个土豆换了朋友的玩具。暴露引来官方调查后，Hanbok把这场不幸变成机会，公开申明他相信间岛实为朝鲜领土。最终，他帮助朝鲜政府找到支持朝鲜对间岛享有领土权利的证据。

children: 〔校注〕小说人物 Hanbok 的汉字在中文研究文献中一作“李翰福”、一作“李汉福”，未定于一（该书尚无华语译本可据），保留罗马转写。

en: The migration to northern Kando represents the survival of the family and the nation. On the one hand, it is literally the final attempt at survival by the impecunious peasants. When migration is prohibited and violators are sentenced to death, the choice for the peasants is between dying of hunger and being executed by the state. On the other hand, the migration to Kando is figuratively the passage to a new Korean nation. Hanbok, a protagonist in Pukkando, was one of the few Koreans who risked his life to farm in Kando. As Kando is located just across the Tuman River from Hanbok’s village in Korea, farming there requires crossing the river daily. He usually sets out for Kando in the dark and returns home before dawn, having farmed throughout the night. Hanbok’s clandestine farming is inadvertently revealed by his son when the boy trades three potatoes for a friend’s toy. When his exposure leads to an official investigation, Hanbok turns this misfortune into an opportunity to aver his belief that Kando is really Korean territory. In the end, he helps the Korean government to establish proof of its territorial right to Kando.

zh: 这片领土的重新取得标志着民族建设的新时期，因为腐败的国家官员已屈服于中国的势力，未能驳斥中国对这片土地数百年之久的主张。Hanbok引领了一波朝鲜移民潮，把这片边疆变成又一个繁荣的村庄。通过取得土地、为孩子们办学，Hanbok化解了延续三代的耕作与教育之争——这场争执在他祖父与父亲之间、以及父亲与他之间播下仇怨。儒家原则把父系家庭——尤其父子世系——视为民族共同体的核心。按儒家思想，治理天下始于修身齐家，国家与人民的理想关系必须映照家长与家庭的天然关系。父子冲突象征民族共同体的崩解，以及随之而来的父系存续威胁。Hanbok家族在间岛化解代际冲突，寓意着这场民族危机的化解。
en: The reacquisition of this territory signifies a new period of nation building, as corrupted state officials have succumbed to the power of China and failed to refute the centuries-old claim of China to this land. Hanbok leads a wave of Korean migration that turns this frontier into yet another flourishing village. By obtaining land and operating schools for children, Hanbok resolves the conflict between farming and education that has spanned three generations and sown enmity between his grandfather and his father, as well as between his father and him. The Confucian principle considers the patrilineal family—especially the father-son lineage—to be the nucleus of the national community. According to Confucianism, rule of the whole world begins with command of one’s own body and family and the ideal relationship between the state and its people must mirror the innate relationship between the patriarch and his family. Father-son conflict symbolizes the breakdown of the national community and subsequent threats to the survival of the patriline. The resolution of generational conflict in Hanbok’s family in Kando connotes the resolution of this national crisis.

zh: 以下对书中三个情节的分析，提供了朝鲜人与中国人、日本人发展出的三种同床者式关系的例证。尽管发生在不同历史语境中，这些情节未必是转瞬即逝的三角关系的编年记录。它们可以被看作共时的变形：民族时间与资本主义时间——尽管资本主义时间往往只在暗处显现——生产出三角关系的不同样式。特定历史语境中的所有事件，都以不同方式把朝鲜人铭写进朝鲜民族的先验空间。他们的民族身份与其资本主义追求——包括维持私有财产权与扩张市场活动——陷入张力。朝鲜人、中国人、日本人之间的第一种三角关系强化了朝鲜民族主义：它在中国因恐惧日本侵蚀满洲、而规定朝鲜人入籍为中国国民作为土地所有权前提时发展起来。朝鲜民族主义与中国民族主义的妥协，产生了变异的入籍与土地所有权形式。第二种三角关系涉及朝鲜与中国民族主义的统一战线，反对中国与朝鲜的腐败国家。这种新的民族与全球意识转化为与物质利益相结合的民众政治。第三种关系围绕中日警察在城市中追捕一名朝鲜重罪犯展开。追捕体现了朝鲜人交换价值的上升、中日领土竞争给他们带来的双重压迫，以及朝鲜人利用这两个对手相互倾轧而争取到的好处。这些好处也可视为朝鲜人劳动力走向商品化的标志——中日两种权力都试图占有这种劳动力，以发展满洲农业。在每一种关系中，国际历史事件与间岛朝鲜人的事件汇聚，戏剧化地呈现朝鲜人作为殖民者与被殖民者的双重位置所催生的主体性新构型。三个情节并非彼此孤立，而是展现三角关系的不同维度。
en: The following analysis of three episodes from the book offers three examples of bedfellow-type relationships that Koreans develop with the Chinese and Japanese. Although they take place in different historical contexts, these episodes are not necessarily a chronicle of fleeting triangular relationships. They can be considered synchronic metamorphoses in which national and capitalist time—though the latter is often suggestive—produce variant modes of the triangular relationship. All of the events within specific historical contexts inscribe Koreans to the a priori space of the Korean nation in different registers. Their national identity is brought into tension with their capitalist pursuits, including the maintenance of private property rights and the expansion of market activities. The first triangular relationship among Koreans, Chinese, and Japanese reinforces Korean nationalism, as it develops when China, fearing Japanese encroachment on Manchuria, stipulates naturalization of Koreans as Chinese nationals as a prerequisite for landownership. The compromise between Korean and Chinese nationalism yields aberrant forms of naturalization and landownership. The second triangular relationship involves the united front of Korean and Chinese nationalisms against the corrupt states of China and Korea. This new national and global consciousness is transformed into a popular politics coupled with material gain. The third relationship revolves around the pursuit by Chinese and Japanese policemen of a Korean felon in a city. The chase represents the increased exchange value of Koreans, their double oppression as a result of the territorial rivalry between China and Japan, and the advantages that Koreans carve out by turning these rivals against each other. These advantages can also be taken as a signifier of the commodification of Korean labor, which both the Chinese and Japanese powers sought to appropriate in order to develop Manchurian agriculture. In each relationship, international historical events coalesce with those of Koreans in Kando to dramatize emergent configurations of Korean subjectivity arising from their dual position as colonizer and colonized. Instead of standing apart from one another, the three episodes exhibit variant dimensions of the triangular relationship.

zh: “土豆故事”：社会生活与民族
en: “Potato Tales”: Social Life and the Nation

zh: 土豆事件的情节提供了朝鲜人与中国人之间新兴对立的第一个场域，这一对立随着日本帝国主义的推进而加速。中国在甲午战争（1894–95）中战败；这场战争因中日两国据称为了镇压东学农民起义而向朝鲜派兵爆发。在1898年于下关签订的条约中，中国承认朝鲜完全独立，并把满洲的辽东半岛与台湾岛割让给日本。
1870年与1881年，朝鲜与中国分别批准本国农民迁移，重新点燃了古老的领土争端。战败后，中国担心日本介入这些领土争端。
清政府因此开始施压间岛朝鲜人入籍为中国公民。

children: 〔校注〕原书印作“1898年于下关签订的条约”；《马关条约》实签于1895年。已核印本页面（assets/pages/p028_treaty_crop.png）确为1898；照印翻译。

en: The episode of the potato incidents offers the first venue for the emergent opposition between Koreans and Chinese, which accelerates as Japanese imperialism advances. China had been defeated in the Sino-Japanese War (1894–95), which broke out when China and Japan sent troops to Korea allegedly to quell the Tonghak peasant rebellion. In the treaty signed at Shimonoseki in 1898, China conceded the full independence of Korea and transferred the Liaodong Peninsula of Manchuria and the island of Taiwan to Japan.

In 1870 and 1881, respectively, authorization of the migration of Korean and Chinese peasants by Korea and China had rekindled age-old territorial disputes. After its defeat in the war, China feared that Japan would intervene in these territorial disputes.
The Qing government therefore began to pressure the Koreans of Kando to become naturalized as Chinese citizens.

zh: 当时，入籍采取强制满族服饰与发式的文化形式（Hŭkpok pyŏnbal，黑服辫发；或 Ch'ibal yŏkpok，剃发易服）——黑衣宽长袖，前额剃发，脑后留长辫。这一满族习俗与朝鲜习俗形成对照：朝鲜人穿白衣，发式依婚姻状况而异——未婚男子前发短、脑后留长辫，已婚男子束发戴于头顶。清当局向朝鲜人争取让步时，把入籍描绘为轻而易举的过程：未婚男子剪去前发、已婚男子解开发髻即可。
《北间岛》写道，许多朝鲜人觉得民族的灵魂“不会宽恕这样的入籍”，因为儒家习俗把头发视为祖先的遗赠。
en: At that time, naturalization took the cultural form (Hŭkpok pyŏnbal or Ch’ibal yŏkpok) of enforcing Manchu clothing and hairstyles—black clothes with wide, long sleeves and hair shaved in front and worn in a long ponytail in back. This Manchu custom contrasts with the Korean practice of wearing white clothes and different hairstyles according to marital status—short hair in front and a long ponytail in back for unmarried men and hair tied and worn on top of the head for married men. In seeking a concession from the Koreans, the Qing authorities presented naturalization as a process as easy as cutting the front hair for unmarried men and untying hair for married men.
Pukkando relates that many Koreans felt that the soul of the nation “would not forgive such naturalization,” since Confucian custom identifies one’s hair as a bequest of the ancestors.

zh: 然而入籍问题超出了民族身份本身。由于清政府把它作为土地所有权的前提，入籍问题关系到朝鲜人对自身社会生活的主权。作为劳动产品，《北间岛》中的土豆象征着生产者的劳动，正是这种劳动增加了土地的价值。对土地的所有权等同于对自身社会生活的主权，因为土地的价值与人投入其上的劳动不可分离。小说的土豆事件描绘了社会生活与民族身份之间的张力——把国籍与土地所有权捆绑在一起的中国法律，把这种张力设定为对立。小说中，入籍问题让朝鲜人陷入棘手的两难：保住民族身份，还是捍卫自己的土地权利。随着中国人与朝鲜人之间紧张加剧，这一困境的加深为一场土豆事件搭好了舞台。玩耍时，Hanbok的孙子Ch'angyun和伙伴们从村里最富有的中国地主的田里偷土豆。Ch'angyun的行动不仅出于对地主的敌意，也出于对朝鲜邻人的蔑视——他们似乎越来越屈从于地主。地主家人通过模拟入籍来训斥Ch'angyun——把他的衣服和发式改成满族样式。

children: 〔校注〕小说人物 Ch'angyun 的汉字在中文研究文献中一作“昌允”、一作“昌润”，未定于一，保留罗马转写。

en: The issue of naturalization, however, exceeded the matter of one’s national identity. As the Qing government required it as a precondition for landownership, the matter of naturalization concerned the sovereignty of Koreans over their social lives. Being products of labor, potatoes in Pukkando symbolize the labor of producers, which increases the value of land. The property rights to one’s land are equivalent to the sovereignty over one’s social life since the value of land is inextricable from the labor one expends on it. The novel’s potato incidents depict the tension between social life and national identity, which is posited as an opposition by the Chinese law that entwined nationality and landownership. In the novel, the issue of naturalization presents Koreans with the thorny dilemma of choosing between keeping their national identity and defending their rights to their lands. A deepening of this predicament, in tandem with mounting tensions between the Chinese and Koreans, sets the stage for a potato incident. During their playtime, Ch’angyun—Hanbok’s grandson—and his friends steal potatoes from a farm owned by the village’s richest Chinese landlord. Ch’angyun’s action is triggered not just by hostility toward the landlord but also by disdain for his Korean neighbors, who increasingly seem to succumb to the landlord. The landlord’s household members reprimand Ch’angyun by simulating his naturalization—changing his clothes and hair to the Manchu style.

zh: Hanbok因这一事件的打击而死，却促成了村里社会生活与入籍之间的妥协。他死前，村民曾为哪一种“爱村之法”最妥当而争论。第一种主张由中国政府推荐：由少数代表入籍，以他们的名义登记未入籍村民耕种的土地。以Hanbok为首的反对派不仅重申间岛是朝鲜领土，还确认朝鲜人对自己土地的所有权：“朝鲜政府无力主张间岛的主权，无论这是因为它软弱还是因为它腐败，我们都不能把洒下自己血汗的土地交给中国。尽管让少数代表入籍是维持我们所有权的务实策略，但这会成为下一代沦为中国人奴隶的根据。”
Hanbok死后，朝鲜人采纳了这一策略：选出代表，创设自己的土地凭证——与中国政府发给名义土地所有人的官方凭证相区别——以区分实际土地所有人与名义土地所有人。当选代表起初帮助朝鲜人与当地中国官员交涉税务及其他法律事务。但正如Hanbok所预言，他们越来越对其他朝鲜人施展权力。
en: Hanbok’s death from the shock over this incident facilitates a compromise between social life and naturalization in his village. Before his death, the villagers had debated the contending positions on the best “method to love the village.” In the first proposition, the one recommended by the Chinese government, a couple of their representatives would become naturalized and register under their names the land tilled by the unnaturalized village members. The opposition, led by Hanbok, not only reinvoked Kando as Korean territory but also affirmed Koreans’ right to ownership of their land: “Regardless of whether the Korean government is too weak or corrupt to claim sovereignty over Kando, it is not feasible for us to give to China the land on which we poured our sweat and blood. Even though the naturalization of a couple of our representatives is a practical strategy to maintain our ownership, it would be grounds for the next generation to become slaves of the Chinese people.”

Adopting this strategy after Hanbok’s death, the Koreans elect their representatives and create their own land title—apart from the official title that the Chinese government had issued to nominal landowners—which will distinguish real and nominal landowners. The elected representatives at first help the Koreans in their negotiations with local Chinese officials over taxation and other legal matters. But, as Hanbok predicted, they increasingly exert power over the other Koreans.

zh: Ch'angyun的土豆事件唤醒了被压抑的早年土豆事件的记忆——那一次涉及他的祖父（Hanbok）与父亲（Changson）迁往间岛之前的岁月——从而把他的家族带回到朝鲜的危机时刻。在重复的土豆事件中，民族秩序与社会秩序交织的危机被铭写在父子关系之上，并由父子关系化解。正如Hanbok当年化解了他祖父与父亲之间的裂隙，Ch'angyun也为他的祖父与父亲做了同样的事。Ch'angyun的事件使Hanbok想起自己非法耕种的往事。Hanbok满怀自豪，但其中夹杂着对再次威胁家族生计的境况的忧惧。对Hanbok随后之死的内疚，使Ch'angyun与最好的朋友打架。他们互相嘲骂，叫对方“中国人”（Ch'angyun曾穿过满族衣服，而朋友的父亲作为村代表已入籍中国）。Ch'angyun从崖上摔下，摔断了脚踝，病倒了。Changson起初责怪儿子愚蠢，但Ch'angyun即使在谵妄中仍流露悔意，使Changson含泪回忆起一件被深深压抑了数十年的往事。多年前，当Changson用土豆换玩具导致父亲被捕时，暴怒的Hanbok曾宣称：“谁向政府告发我在间岛耕种，我就杀谁，哪怕是我的孩子。”Changson如今猜想，从第一次土豆事件中得到的教训，必定养成了在间岛生存所需的坚韧与决心。Ch'angyun的土豆事件似乎为家族中延续一代人的紧张、以及村里围绕入籍的冲突画上了句号。

children: 〔校注〕小说人物 Changson（Hanbok 之子、Ch'angyun 之父）汉字未核实，保留罗马转写。

en: Ch’angyun’s potato incident brings his family back to the time of crisis in Korea by resuscitating the repressed memory of an earlier potato incident, one that involved his grandfather (Hanbok) and father (Changson) before their migration to Kando. In the repeated potato incidents, the crisis of the entwined national and social order is encoded on and resolved by the father-son relationship. As Hanbok once resolved the schism between his grandfather and father, Ch’angyun does the same for his grandfather and father. Ch’angyun’s incident causes Hanbok to remember his own saga of illegal farming. Hanbok is overcome with pride, but it is mixed with apprehension over the conditions that are once again threatening the family’s livelihood. Guilt over Hanbok’s subsequent death induces Ch’angyun to fight with his best friend. They mock each other, calling each other “Chinese” (Ch’angyun once wore Manchu clothes and the father of his friend has adopted Chinese naturalization in his role as a village representative). Ch’angyun breaks his ankle after falling from a cliff and becomes ill. While Changson at first blames his son for his foolishness, Ch’angyun’s remorse, even in delirium, leads Changson to a tearful reminiscence of an event that had been deeply suppressed for decades. Years ago, when Changson’s trading of the potatoes for a toy led to the arrest of his father, the enraged Hanbok declared that he would “kill whoever reported my farming in Kando to the government, even my child.” Changson now suspects that the lesson learned from this first potato incident must have nurtured the perseverance and determination necessary to survive in Kando. Ch’angyun’s potato incident seems to bring closure to a generation-long tension in his family, as well as the conflict in the village over naturalization.

zh: 三代人之间土豆情节的重复，象征着朝鲜民族同质而连续的时间，而这一时间也带有微妙的含混。民族时间把间岛的朝鲜人与朝鲜民族绑定在一起。土豆事件体现了朝鲜移民在民族时间之内维持自身社会生活的持续斗争。在《北间岛》中，这种斗争的重复进一步被以下事实强化：当年用玩具诱惑Ch'angyun父亲的那位童年伙伴，如今成了入籍的村代表；而这位伙伴的儿子，正是导致Ch'angyun坠崖的人。由下一代辩证地化解父子冲突，标志着民族时间的运作——它把农民与民族的统一自然化。当村民谴责朝鲜国家连臣民穿自己衣服的权利都保护不了时，父系摩擦的化解意味着《北间岛》的作者仍保留民族自身的能动性：号召农民移民调和其社会生活与民族身份。然而《北间岛》叙事中民族的这种作用仍不完整。施加在朝鲜人身体上的痛苦——Hanbok之死、Ch'angyun的断踝与疾病——意味着移民的经验无法被民族时间容纳。村民与入籍代表之间日益加剧的冲突，预示着家族、共同体与民族的新危机。Hanbok之死暗示旧民族时间的终结与新民族时间的开启。
en: The repetition of potato episodes over three generations signifies the homogeneous and continuous time of the Korean nation, which is also marked by subtle ambiguity. National time binds the Koreans of Kando to the Korean nation. The potato incidents embody the persistent struggle of Korean migrants to maintain their social life within national time. In Pukkando, the repetition of the struggle is further accentuated by the fact that a childhood friend who tempted Ch’angyun’s father with a toy is now a village representative who becomes naturalized, and that this friend’s son is responsible for Ch’angyun’s fall from the cliff. The dialectical resolution of the father-son conflict by the succeeding generation denotes the working of national time, which naturalizes the unity of peasants and the nation. When the villagers condemn the Korean state for failing even to protect their subjects’ right to wear their own clothes, the resolution of the patrilineal friction implies that the author of Pukkando still preserves the agency of the nation itself in calling on the peasant migrants to reconcile their social life and national identity. Yet this work of the nation in the narratives of Pukkando remains incomplete. The pain inflicted on Korean bodies—Hanbok’s death and Ch’angyun’s broken ankle and illness—implies that the experience of the migrants cannot be contained by national time. The growing clash between the villagers and their naturalized representatives foretells a new crisis for the family, community, and nation. Hanbok’s death intimates the end of the old national time and the inauguration of a new one.

zh: “你们和我们是一样的”：朝鲜人与中国人的民众统一战线
en: “You and We Are the Same”: A Popular United Front of Koreans and Chinese

zh: 这一情节描绘了间岛、朝鲜与中国的一种新民族时间，它与资本主义时间交织在一起。入籍问题在这里被重构为一种民众政治：朝鲜人的物质关切在日常生活中把朝鲜民族主义与中国民族主义绑定在一起。事件的展开始于1905年日俄条约为日本向满洲与朝鲜推进打开大门。甲午战争后，俄国对满洲与朝鲜发动军事攻击。它从中国取得若干权利，并于1895年迫使日本把辽东半岛归还中国。俄国获准修建穿过满洲的西伯利亚大铁路东段，租借辽东半岛的旅顺与大连，以铁路连接这两大港口，并把它们接入西伯利亚干线。利用1900年中国义和团运动的政治危机，俄国派兵满洲准备占领。俄国还威胁朝鲜，施压日本撤军并接受把北纬三十九度线以北的朝鲜划为不受外国势力支配的中立地带的提议。1904年与英国、美国结盟对俄开战后，日本于1905年与俄国签订《朴茨茅斯条约》，据此接管俄国在南满的一切权利与特权，包括辽东半岛的租借权。该半岛被划为关东租借地，成为日本渗透满洲的基地。日本作出的唯一让步是一项妥协：同意只保留库页岛（萨哈林）南半部的控制权。

children: 〔校注〕原书称日本1904年“与英国、美国结盟对俄开战”；史实为日英同盟，美国并未与日结盟，疑原书有误；照印翻译。

en: This episode depicts a new national time in Kando, Korea, and China, which is entwined with capitalist time. The issue of naturalization is reconfigured here into a popular politics, one in which Koreans’ material concerns bind Korean with Chinese nationalism in everyday life. Events began to unfold when the Russo-Japanese Treaty of 1905 opened the door for Japan’s advance on Manchuria and Korea. After the Sino-Japanese War, Russia launched military attacks on Manchuria and Korea. It acquired a number of rights from China and forced Japan to return the Liaodong Peninsula to China in 1895. Russia was permitted to build the eastern portion of the Trans-Siberian Railway through Manchuria, to lease Port Arthur and Dairen on the Liaodong Peninsula, to link these two major ports by rail, and to connect them both to the Trans-Siberian line. Exploiting the political crisis of the Boxer uprising in China in 1900, Russia dispatched its army to Manchuria to prepare for its occupation. Russia also threatened Korea, pressuring Japan to withdraw its forces and accept the proposition that Korea above the thirty-ninth parallel be designated as a neutral zone free from foreign powers. After allying itself with England and the United States to wage war against Russia in 1904, Japan signed the Portsmouth Treaty with Russia in 1905, under which it assumed all Russian rights and privileges in South Manchuria, including the lease of the Liaodong Peninsula. Designated the Kwantung Leased Territory, the peninsula became the base for Japanese penetration into Manchuria. The only concession offered by Japan was a compromise in which it agreed to retain control of only the southern half of the island of Sakhalin.

zh: 在《北间岛》中，俄国入侵满洲期间，朝鲜本土与满洲的朝鲜人支持俄国，以期击败中国与日本。当间岛的中国官员与地主为躲避俄国攻击而逃离满洲时，朝鲜人摆脱了中国的入籍压力。与俄国紧密结盟的朝鲜政府再次宣称间岛为其领土，派遣专员管理朝鲜人。但日本在日俄战争中的胜利，随之带来中国官员与地主的回归，以及间岛入籍政策的恢复。这一变化与朝鲜及日本的其他关键转变结合在一起。日本迫使朝鲜于1905年签订《保护条约》，而日本的扩张促使中国革命运动兴起。
en: In Pukkando, Koreans in Korea and Manchuria support Russia during the Russian invasion of Manchuria so as to defeat China and Japan. When Chinese officials and landlords in Kando flee Manchuria to escape Russian attacks, the Koreans are freed of the Chinese pressure to become naturalized. Again claiming Kando as its territory, the Korean government, closely allied with Russia, dispatches a commissioner to administer the Koreans. But Japan’s victory in the Russo-Japanese War is followed by the return of Chinese officials and landlords and the resumption of the policy of naturalization in Kando. This change combines with other critical transformations in Korea and Japan. Japan forces Korea to sign the Protectorate Treaty in 1905, and Japan’s encroachment drives the revolutionary movement in China.

zh: “你们和我们是一样的”（Tangsinnewa urinŭn katta）一章描绘了朝鲜人与中国人之间为反对日本侵蚀而结成的新兴统一战线政治。标题中的“一样”代表朝鲜人与中国人共享的新全球意识——共享一个侵蚀朝鲜与中国领土主权的共同殖民者。这一全球视角由间岛朝鲜人的新社会意识所促成，后者通过Ch'angyun的经历得到描绘。回朝鲜祖父故乡的一次旅行，给了Ch'angyun区分朝鲜与间岛朝鲜人的机会。踏上朝鲜土地时，Ch'angyun被对朝鲜人的羡慕压倒。在他最初的印象里，朝鲜的土地、人民与生活方式比间岛更本真。如果说野兽与盗贼的恐怖与威胁定义了间岛的自然环境，那么朝鲜则是“安宁与舒适栖居于树木与森林之中”。“[朝鲜]故乡的空气更温柔，天空是更清澈的蓝。”
朝鲜人单薄的衣衫在Ch'angyun看来比他自己厚重的棉装更时髦。然而，当Ch'angyun看到亲戚们遭受的绝望与苦难时，这一比较立刻反转而偏向间岛。如果他曾经因间岛同村人皮肤黝黑——长时间烈日劳作的结果——而轻视他们，那么此刻Ch'angyun欣赏他们的勤劳与彼此信任。他喃喃道：“无论如何，还是我们的[间岛的社会生活]最好。”
他在间岛苦难的辛酸记忆转化为成就感。
en: The chapter “You and We Are the Same” (Tangsinnewa urinŭn katta) depicts the emergent politics of the united front forged between Koreans and Chinese against Japanese encroachment. The word same in the title represents the new global consciousness shared by Koreans and Chinese—the sharing of a common colonizer that encroaches on the territorial sovereignty of Korea and China. This global viewpoint is enabled by the new social consciousness of Koreans in Kando, which is portrayed through Ch’angyun’s experiences. A trip to his grandfather’s hometown in Korea provides Ch’angyun with the opportunity to distinguish Korea and the Koreans of Kando. When he steps onto the soil of Korea, Ch’angyun is overwhelmed by envy of people in Korea. In his initial impression, the land, people, and lifestyle in Korea are more authentic than in Kando. Whereas horror and menace by beasts and thieves define Kando’s natural setting, “peace and comfort dwell in trees and forests” in Korea. “The air is tender and the sky is a more lucid blue in the [Korean] hometown.”

The thinly layered clothing of the Koreans appears to Ch’angyun to be more stylish than his own heavily padded attire. However, this comparison is instantly reversed to favor Kando when Ch’angyun observes the despair and hardship suffered by his relatives. If he once denigrated his fellow villagers in Kando for their dark skin, the result of long hours toiling under the sun, Ch’angyun now appreciates their diligence and trust in one another. He mutters, “no matter what, ours [social life in Kando] is the best.”
His bitter memories of hardship in Kando turn into a sense of achievement.

zh: 对“我们的”的确认，凸显了间岛朝鲜人的一种新社会意识：承认他们累积劳动的价值，以及拥有吸收这些劳动的土地的权利。这种社会意识建立在间岛朝鲜人与朝鲜本土朝鲜人之间的差异之上，而这些差异并不必然导向矛盾与对立。它意味着间岛朝鲜人的社会经验无法被民族划定的同质化与领土化框架完全涵盖。正是从这一差异的位置出发，Ch'angyun在朝鲜的朝鲜人与中国人之间斡旋，锻造新的民族与全球意识：“朝鲜人和中国人是一样的。”也正是通过与他从前的朝鲜老师Cho先生、以及被囚禁的中国革命者王先生（Mr. Wang）的带有教诲意味的谈话，Ch'angyun试图把自己的社会意识与新的中国及朝鲜民族主义调和——后者要求在反日斗争中进行全球合作。Cho先生是正在消失的那类儒学者之一，曾反对朝日《保护条约》。他告诫Ch'angyun：间岛朝鲜人的敌人不再是中国人，而是日本人与俄国人；朝鲜人与中国人必须学会合作。俄国尽管被日本击败，却与日本共享殖民朝鲜与中国的野心。Ch'angyun很容易理解朝鲜人必须阻止日本侵蚀，但他对克服间岛朝鲜人与中国人之间的仇怨表示疑虑。翌日清晨Cho先生被发现死亡时，Ch'angyun“愿意相信”他是自杀，相信他对统一战线的呼吁是留给Ch'angyun的遗赠。决心践行这份遗赠，Ch'angyun努力压抑自己对中国人根深蒂固的敌意。

children: 〔校注〕小说人物 Cho 先生汉字未核实（或为赵/曹），保留转写；王先生按拼音还原为王。

en: Recognizing “ours” foregrounds a new social consciousness among Koreans in Kando in recognition of the worth of their accumulated labor and their right to own the land that absorbs it. This social consciousness rests on differences between the Koreans of Kando and Korea that do not necessarily lead to contradiction and opposition. It means that the social experiences of the Koreans of Kando escape the homogenizing and territorializing parameters of the nation. It is from this position of difference that Ch’angyun mediates between the Koreans of Korea and the Chinese to forge a new national and global consciousness: “Koreans and Chinese are the same.” It is also through didactic conversations with his former Korean teacher, Mr. Cho, and an imprisoned Chinese revolutionary, Mr. Wang, that Ch’angyun attempts to reconcile his social consciousness with the new Chinese and Korean nationalisms that entail global cooperation in the struggle against Japan. Mr. Cho is one of the vanishing breed of Confucian scholars who opposed the Protectorate Treaty between Korea and Japan. He advises Ch’angyun that the enemies of Koreans in Kando are no longer Chinese but Japanese and Russian and that Koreans and Chinese must learn to cooperate. Despite its defeat by Japan, Russia shares with it the aspiration to colonize Korea and China. Whereas it is easy for Ch’angyun to understand that Koreans must prevent Japanese encroachment, he expresses misgivings about overcoming the animosity between the Koreans of Kando and the Chinese. When Mr. Cho is found dead the next morning, Ch’angyun “wants to believe” that his death was a suicide and that his appeal for the united front was his legacy to Ch’angyun. Determined to honor it, Ch’angyun tries to suppress his deep-seated hostility toward the Chinese.

zh: Ch'angyun对与中国人结盟的疑虑，因与中国革命者王先生的相遇而部分化解。回到村里后，Ch'angyun被捕，罪名是他俄军入侵满洲期间组织的朝鲜自卫团体与中国革命渗透者之间有牵连。此时距1911年中华民国建立尚有五六年，王先生是一位来自华南的革命者。同囚一室，两人在夜间断续交谈。王先生安慰在审讯中遭受酷刑的Ch'angyun，告诉他：尽管狱吏是贼，“但我们中国人并不都坏”，“还是好人多”。王先生接着重复Cho先生说过的话：“中国人和朝鲜人是一样的。”在Ch'angyun心里，Cho先生所说的贼是日本，王先生所说的贼是暴虐的清政府。
en: Ch’angyun’s doubts about an alliance with the Chinese are partially resolved by his encounter with a Chinese revolutionary, Mr. Wang. Returning to his village, Ch’angyun is arrested for an alleged link between a Korean self-defense group, which he organized during the Russian invasion of Manchuria, and Chinese revolutionary infiltrators. At this point, five or six years before the establishment of Republican China in 1911, Mr. Wang is a revolutionary from South China. Sharing the same prison cell, the two men intermittently converse during the night. Consoling Ch’angyun, who was tortured during his interrogation, Mr. Wang tells him that although the prison officials are thieves “all our Chinese people are not bad” and “there are more good people.” Mr. Wang then repeats what Mr. Cho stated: “Chinese and Koreans are the same.” In Ch’angyun’s mind, Mr. Cho’s thief is Japan and Mr. Wang’s is the tyrannical Qing government.

zh: 革命的中国民族主义通过把日本与清政府指认为共同敌人，克服了中国人与朝鲜人（无论朝鲜本土还是间岛的朝鲜人）之间此前的对立。Ch'angyun意识到清政府也是间岛朝鲜人的敌人。对Ch'angyun而言，这个政府配得上被朝鲜人称为贼，因为它“宣称别人[朝鲜人]的土地是自己的土地。宣称别人的人民是自己的人民，还强迫他们编辫子、穿它自己的服装样式。这些对朝鲜人犯下的罪行，足以使它成为贼。”
在两人共处的最后一夜，王先生指出，在中国人眼中日本同样是贼。
Ch'angyun与王先生互相告诉对方：“朝鲜人和中国人是一样的。”当王先生终于要展开阐述自己的思想时，谈话被狱卒打断——狱卒叫王先生出去，秘密处决他。这位革命者深深触动了他，Ch'angyun重复Cho先生与王先生的话：“朝鲜人和中国人是一样的。”
en: Revolutionary Chinese nationalism overcomes the previous antagonism between Chinese and Koreans (of both Korea and Kando) by identifying Japan and the Qing government as their common enemies. Ch’angyun realizes that the Qing government is also the enemy of the Koreans of Kando. For Ch’angyun, the government deserves to be called a thief by Koreans, for it “asserts that others’ [Koreans’] land is its own land. Asserting others’ people as its own people, it also forced them to braid their hair and wear its own clothing styles. These crimes against Koreans are sufficient to make it a thief.”
On their final night together, Mr. Wang observes that Japan is also a thief in the eyes of the Chinese people.

Ch’angyun and Mr. Wang tell each other that “Koreans and Chinese are the same.” As Mr. Wang is finally about to expand on his thoughts, the conversation is interrupted by a prison guard, who calls Mr. Wang for his clandestine execution. Overwhelmed by empathy for this revolutionary, Ch’angyun repeats the phrase of Mr. Cho and Mr. Wang: “Koreans and Chinese are the same.”

zh: 间岛朝鲜人萌芽中的社会、民族与全球意识，似乎类似于从资本主义、民族与殖民压迫中真正同时解放所必需的乌托邦式革命公式。Ch'angyun的社会意识蕴含着关于殖民权力与朝鲜、中国腐败民族政府的新民族与全球意识。他的社会意识导向一种朝鲜的民族与全球意识：他认同朝鲜本土的朝鲜人与满洲和中国本部的中国人，但同时承认间岛朝鲜人的独特经验。间岛朝鲜人的这种独特性，暴露了把他们与朝鲜或中国同质化的不可能。早先的朝鲜与中国民族主义把间岛朝鲜人纳入自身：把间岛视为朝鲜的延伸（拒绝其入籍为中国国民），或视为中国的延伸（强迫朝鲜人成为中国人）。Ch'angyun的社会意识如今能够设想一种不要求同化的、与朝鲜本土朝鲜人及中国人的联盟。如果这种社会意识开花结果，它就能引领朝鲜与中国的“人民”投入新的民族与全球斗争。新的全球联盟要求超越在领土、习俗与传统上的民族差异。它必须包含对殖民主义、民族主义与资本主义的同时批判——正是三者复杂的相互作用，把朝鲜、间岛与中国的劳动者逐出土地。
en: The embryonic social, national, and global consciousness of Koreans in Kando appears to be analogous to the utopian and revolutionary formula necessary for genuine, simultaneous liberation from capitalist, national, and colonial oppression. Ch’angyun’s social consciousness entails a new national and global consciousness about colonial power and the corrupt national governments of Korea and China. His social consciousness leads to a Korean national and global consciousness in which he identifies with the Koreans of Korea and the Chinese of Manchuria and China but nevertheless acknowledges the distinctive experiences of the Koreans of Kando. This distinction of Koreans in Kando exposes the impossibility of homogenizing them with either Korea or China. Earlier Korean and Chinese nationalisms subsumed the Koreans of Kando by regarding Kando as an extension of Korea (by refusing naturalization as Chinese nationals) and China (by forcing Koreans to become Chinese nationals). Ch’angyun’s social consciousness is now capable of envisioning an alliance with the Koreans of Korea and the Chinese that will not require assimilation. If this social consciousness were to blossom, it could lead the Korean and Chinese “people” in a new national and global struggle. The new global alliance requires transcendence of national differences over territory, customs, and traditions. It must entail a simultaneous critique of colonialism, nationalism, and capitalism, whose complex interactions expel the laborers of Korea, Kando, and China from the land.

zh: 一种能把朝鲜人与中国人从民族主义与殖民压迫中解放出来的可行全球意识，不仅必须处理被殖民者之间的共性，还必须处理被压迫者与压迫者内部及之间的差异与等级。但同质化的民族主义使这种可能性变得不确定。尽管Ch'angyun对间岛朝鲜人社会独特性的承认，为朝鲜人与中国人组成的统一战线奠定了基础，他的社会意识仍持续被他对Cho先生与王先生的共情所压抑。在“你们和我们是一样的”这句话中，“你们”与“我们”这两个范畴指民族共同体——朝鲜与中国。“我们”这一范畴把间岛并入朝鲜，把朝鲜本土与间岛的朝鲜人同质化为“韩国人”（Han'gugin）。Cho先生与王先生的民族意识仍绑定于领土与族群的同质性。尽管两人都承认间岛朝鲜人生活的独特价值，但无论Cho先生还是Ch'angyun，都没有把这种平等关系扩展到朝鲜与间岛之间。当Ch'angyun表达对统一战线的疑虑时，他很快将 Cho 先生的呼吁视为应当继承的遗愿，把这些疑虑压了下去。这种被压下的对中国的疑虑或敌意，象征着新民族与全球意识的不完整性。Ch'angyun与中国囚犯之间被打断的谈话，也是这种不充分意识的隐喻。尽管具有开创性，Ch'angyun对朝鲜与间岛之区别的洞见，未能把“我们”或“韩国人”（Han'gugin）这一单一范畴问题化。
en: A viable global consciousness capable of liberating Koreans and Chinese from nationalist and colonial oppression must address not just commonalities among the colonized but also the differences and hierarchy within and between the oppressed and the oppressors. But homogenizing nationalism renders this possibility indefinite. Although Ch’angyun’s recognition of the social distinction of Koreans of Kando lays the groundwork for a united front composed of Koreans and Chinese, Ch’angyun’s social consciousness continues to be suppressed by his empathy for Mr. Cho and Mr. Wang. In the phrase, “you and we are the same,” the categories “you” and “we” refer to national communities—Korea and China. Annexing Kando to Korea, the category “we” homogenizes the Koreans of both Korea and Kando as “Korean” (Han’gugin). The national consciousness of Mr. Cho and Mr. Wang remains bound to territorial and ethnic homogeneity. Although both recognize the distinctive value of Korean life in Kando, neither Mr. Cho nor Ch’angyun extends this egalitarian relationship to Korea and Kando. When Ch’angyun expresses his doubts about the united front, he quickly displaces them by embracing Mr. Cho’s appeal as his legacy. This subdued doubt or hostility toward the Chinese symbolizes the incomplete nature of the new national and global consciousness. The interrupted conversation between Ch’angyun and the Chinese prisoner is also a metaphor for this insufficient consciousness. Though groundbreaking, Ch’angyun’s insight into the distinction between Korea and Kando fails to problematize the singular category of “we” or “Han’gugin.”

zh: 资本主义时间进一步搅动了萌芽中的社会、民族与全球意识的感知。它在统一战线向民众意识的变形过程中运作。在《北间岛》中，据说朝鲜人与中国人的团结在朝中农民之间口口相传。尽管此前朝鲜人与中国人之间的小冲突常常导致无情斗殴，如今他们却一笑化解，说“你和我是一样的”。这种民众情感由一个涉及中朝之间物质与政治妥协的有趣事件所巩固。Ch'angyun的村民被哄劝着与中国国家及一位地主达成一项涉及全村的协议，把他们的民众意识与物质利益结合起来。他们感兴趣的是把地方政府衙门设到自己的村里。这在几年前还不可想象，如今却由他们发展村庄经济的愿望所促成——因为村庄变为行政中心有望扩大市场活动。但当最大的中国地主与朝鲜人代表要求村民向间岛地方政府提交集体请愿时，他们犹豫了，害怕从此屈从于中国政府。他们在心里问：“我们怎能以这种方式结束与中国权力数代人之久的斗争？”
最终，经济动力迫使他们同意请愿运动。当土匪偷走村里大部分牛——朝鲜人必不可少的耕畜——时，中国地主给村民贷款买新牛。尽管中国地主对贷款收取高息，村民发现自己不得不支持把政府衙门引进本村的努力。村里一度洋溢着节日气氛，但与此同时，朝鲜人内部的冲突却在加剧。
en: Capitalist time further unsettles the sensibility of the nascent social, national, and global consciousness. It operates during the metamorphosis of the united front into popular consciousness. In Pukkando, the unity of Koreans and Chinese is said to spread from mouth to mouth among Korean and Chinese peasants. Though petty conflicts between Koreans and Chinese often led to ruthless fights before, they now resolve them with laughter, saying, “you and I are the same.” This popular sentiment is consolidated by an intriguing event involving a material and political compromise between Chinese and Koreans. Ch’angyun’s villagers are cajoled into a general compact with the Chinese state and a landlord, coupling their popular consciousness with material gain. They are interested in bringing the local government office to their village. Unthinkable even a few years ago, this idea is fostered by their desire for economic development in their village, as the transformation of the village as an administrative center is expected to expand market activities. But when the largest Chinese landlord and the Korean representatives ask the villagers to submit a collective petition to the district government of Kando, they hesitate for fear of becoming subordinate to the Chinese government. In their minds, they ask, “How could we end the generations long struggle with Chinese power in this manner?”

In the end, economic dynamics impel them to consent to the petition drive. When bandits steal most of the village’s oxen—essential farming animals for Koreans—the Chinese landlord grants the villagers loans to purchase new ones. Even though the Chinese landlord charges a high rate of interest for the loans, the villagers find themselves obliged to support the efforts to bring the government office to their village. Festive moods prevail in the village for a while, though in a parallel development there are growing conflicts among the Koreans themselves.

zh: 朝鲜农民的社会与物质关切，让这种民众意识演变为在不知不觉中接受中国权力的同化。结果，Ch'angyun村里开设的中国地方衙门，由一名入籍的朝鲜人代表出任首长。该衙门还与一所朝鲜人小学共用空间。《北间岛》中这种把朝鲜民族身份转置为中国身份的做法，有力地暴露了朝鲜人与中国人反对日本帝国主义的民众民族与全球意识中的权力关系。这里隐含的民族时间与资本主义时间的相互作用，在下一个情节中进一步得到象征。
en: The social and material concerns of the Korean peasants transpose a popular consciousness into a state of insensate assimilation by Chinese power. It turns out that after the Chinese local office is opened in Ch’angyun’s village a naturalized Korean representative becomes its head. The office also shares the space with a Korean primary school. This transposition of a Korean national identity into a Chinese one in Pukkando powerfully exposes the power relations in the popular national and global consciousness of Koreans and Chinese against Japanese imperialism. The interplay of national and capitalist time implied here is further symbolized in the next episode.

zh: “我们的身价一定涨了”：朝鲜人的交换价值
en: “Our Value Must Have Increased”: The Exchange Value of Koreans

zh: 在这一情节中，朝鲜人的价值由中日之间的领土竞争——以及暗示中的资本主义竞争——所决定。历史语境是1909年前后日本对间岛的渗透。1907年解散朝鲜军队后，日本在间岛最大城市龙井（Ryongjŏng）设立面向朝鲜人的警察派出所，名义上是保护“朝鲜人的生命与财产”。旨在解决中国与朝鲜（此时由日本代表）之间领土争端的1909年中日《间岛协约》包含三项重要条款：日本承认间岛为中国的一部分；作为回报，中国允许日本在间岛四个主要城市设立领事馆；中国授予朝鲜人在间岛居住与拥有财产的权利，而无需成为中国公民。《间岛协约》未能解决领土争端，更谈不上约束日本对该地区的殖民。日本继续侵蚀中国主权，宣称这是保护朝鲜人生命财产所必需。
en: In this episode, the value of Koreans is determined by territorial and, it is suggested, capitalist competition between China and Japan. The historical context is the penetration of Kando by Japan around 1909. After dissolving the Korean armies in 1907, Japan had created a Korean police substation in Ryongjŏng, the largest city in Kando, ostensibly to protect the “lives and property of Koreans.” Intended to settle the territorial disputes between China and Korea (now represented by Japan), the 1909 Kando treaty between China and Japan included three important clauses: Japan recognized Kando as part of China; China, in return, permitted Japan to establish consulates in four major cities in Kando; and China granted Koreans the right to reside and own property in Kando without becoming Chinese citizens. The Kando Treaty fell short of resolving the territorial disputes, let alone constraining Japanese colonization of the region. Japan continued to encroach on Chinese sovereignty, claiming that this was necessary to guard the lives and property of Koreans.

zh: 在《北间岛》中，《间岛协约》巩固了朝鲜人横跨中国、朝鲜（及日本）主权的矛盾位置。日本以保护朝鲜人为名在龙井设立警察派出所后，中国人开始谴责朝鲜人是日本帝国主义的先锋。中国重申对间岛的主权，重新推行入籍政策并增加军事存在，尽管其兵力不及日军。一些朝鲜人把中国人对朝鲜人日益加剧的压迫归咎于日本警察署，另一些人则开始把日本视为保护者。警察署开设后，逃避中国压迫的难民开始迁往该城。即使在Ch'angyun的村里，当中国官员在追查一名中国人被害案时威胁朝鲜人，日本的帮助也被作为一种选项加以讨论。
en: In Pukkando, the Kando Treaty consolidates the contradictory position of the Koreans that straddled Chinese and Korean (and Japanese) sovereignties. After Japan establishes its police substation in Ryongjong in the name of protecting Koreans, the Chinese begin to condemn Koreans as the forerunners of Japanese imperialism. Reiterating its sovereignty over Kando, China reimposes its naturalization policy and increases its military presence, although its forces are inferior to those of the Japanese. Some Koreans hold the Japanese police station accountable for growing Korean oppression by the Chinese, while others begin to think of Japan as their protector. After the station is opened, refugees from the Chinese oppression begin to migrate to the city. Even in Ch’angyun’s village, Japan’s help is discussed as an option when Chinese officials threaten Koreans in their search for the murderer of a Chinese man.

zh: 题为“我们的身价一定涨了”（Urido kapsi orŭn sem）的情节发生在1909年的龙井。此时该城是间岛的主要商业中心，附近村庄的粮食汇集于此卖给商人。街道与市集店铺林立，已成为间岛商品化与城市化的标志。Ch'angyun在访友时目睹了中日警察争抢逮捕一名朝鲜人的场面。一名日本警察押着一名朝鲜重罪犯——此人身穿清服（ch'ŏngbok），曾在市集参与非法赌博。朝鲜重罪犯与日本警察被一群中国警察追赶。中国警察逼近后，试图从日本人手中抢走被捕的朝鲜人。一名中国警察夺下绑住朝鲜赌徒双手与腰身的绳子。另两人试图按住罪犯。为阻止中国人抢走重罪犯，日本警察朝天鸣枪。就在那一刻，朝鲜人趁乱逃脱。中日警察现在一起追赶这名朝鲜人。《北间岛》如此解释这一事件：“日本警察逮捕朝鲜人，是因为后者尽管穿着清服仍是朝鲜人；而中国警察试图从日本警察手中抢走他，是因为他违反了中国法律。”
en: The episode, entitled “Our Value Must Have Increased” (Urido kapsi orŭn sem), takes place in Ryongjŏng in 1909. At this time, the city is the principal commercial center of Kando, as grain from nearby villages is gathered there and sold to merchants. Lined with stores, its streets and markets have become an emblem of commodification and urbanization in Kando. While visiting a friend, Ch’angyun witnesses a scene in which Japanese and Chinese policemen compete to arrest a Korean. A Japanese policeman is escorting a Korean felon, who, dressed in Chinese clothes (ch’ŏngbok), was involved in illegal gambling in the market. The Korean felon and Japanese policeman are chased by a group of Chinese policemen. Narrowing the chase, the Chinese policemen attempt to snatch the arrested Korean from the Japanese. One Chinese wrests away the rope that binds the hands and waist of the Korean gambler. Two others try to hold the criminal. To deter the Chinese from stealing the felon, a Japanese policeman fires gunshots in the air. In that moment, the Korean takes advantage of the chaos and escapes. Chinese and Japanese policemen are now running after the Korean. As Pukkando explains this event: “The Japanese policeman arrested the Korean since the latter was Korean despite his Chinese clothes, while Chinese policemen tried to steal him from the Japanese policeman because he violated Chinese law.”

zh: 这场追捕集中体现了日中之间的竞争。它抬高了朝鲜人的交换价值，仿佛他们是待价而沽的商品。《北间岛》以Ch'angyun与朋友Hyŏndo阐发的两种相反含义来表象朝鲜人的交换价值——朝鲜人遭受的支配和争取到的好处。对Hyŏndo而言，赌徒的逃脱被视为朝鲜人在竞争中占了上风。用他的话说，“从两队警察的争斗中得利的只有朝鲜人”，
而日中争夺朝鲜人的竞争“提高了我们民族的身价”。
原来，赌徒起初之所以投靠日本警察，是因为那警察其实是朝鲜人。Hyŏndo对一个朝鲜人辜负另一个朝鲜人的信任感到沮丧。但他很快掩饰失望，说“这年头说日本领事馆坏话的人很多，那故事一定是他们编的”。
相反，对Ch'angyun而言，朝鲜人身价的上涨使他们的压迫加倍，因为朝鲜赌徒被日方朝鲜警员和中国权力机关双方出卖。于是，朝鲜人必须忍受做日本帝国主义与中国统治的双重受害者。压迫的代价上升了，因为两国之间的竞争迅速压缩了朝鲜人无需取得中国国籍即可耕种的缝隙空间。

children: 〔校注〕小说人物 Hyŏndo 汉字未核实，保留罗马转写。

en: The chase epitomizes the competition between Japan and China. It increased the exchange value of Koreans, as if they were commodities to be purchased by the highest bidder. Pukkando represents the exchange value of Koreans in terms of two contrary meanings that Ch’angyun and his friend, Hyŏndo, elaborate—the subjugation and advantages of Koreans. For Hyŏndo, the escape of the gambler is seen as advancing Koreans in the competition. In his words, “it is only the Korean who benefits from the fight between two groups of policemen,”
and the competition between Japan and China in courting Koreans “increases the worth of our people.”

It turns out that the gambler initially took shelter with the Japanese policeman because the policeman was actually Korean. Hyŏndo is dismayed that a Korean defied the trust of another Korean. But he quickly hides his disappointment, saying that “these days, there are a lot of people who speak badly of Japanese consulates and they must have made up the story.”

In contrast, for Ch’angyun the increased value of Koreans doubles their oppression, as the Korean gambler was betrayed by both the Korean-Japanese and Chinese powers. Thus, Koreans must endure being the victims of Japanese imperialism and Chinese domination. The price of oppression rises, as the competition between the two countries rapidly reduces the interstitial space where Koreans have been able to farm without adopting Chinese citizenship.

zh: 沿着Ch'angyun的视角，民族时间在《北间岛》中叙述朝鲜人的双重位置。民族主义熟悉的线性修辞规定以压迫与抵抗来描绘朝鲜人的经验，目标是解放朝鲜。故事的叙事策略并置Ch'angyun与其子Chŏngsu所走的两条相连路径：Ch'angyun的不断流离，与Chŏngsu的受教育及参加非共产主义抵抗。当Ch'angyun村里的人无法指认死去中国人的凶手时，中国官员对全村科以罚金。被加剧的紧张与惩罚所困，又被他乡更好生活的传闻所驱动，朝鲜人开始迁移。《北间岛》如此描述这次迁移：“一家，两家，他们毫不犹豫地离开Pibongch'on村，前往能过上好日子的地方。这是一种风。一种狂风。被那风驱赶着，Pibongch'on的人们一家一家带着褴褛的希望前行。”

有些人前往城市、新矿业城镇或俄国。另一些人去满洲北部山区耕种。在辗转迁移中，Ch'angyun一家靠在城市开面馆、制砖、重新耕种、再开面馆糊口。朝鲜人勇敢的抵抗与这条流离叙事交织在一起。被从土地与家庭连根拔起后，Ch'angyun 的兄弟在城里竭力谋生，却比 Ch'angyun 更难立足。他最终加入独立军去解放朝鲜，并战死沙场。与Ch'angyun的兄弟不同，Ch'angyun的儿子受了教育，以教师为业获得稳定生计，但也参加反日解放运动。

children: 〔校注〕Chŏngsu（Ch'angyun 之子）与村名 Pibongch'on 汉字未核实，保留罗马转写。

en: Along the lines of Ch’angyun’s perspective, national time narrates the double position of Koreans in Pukkando. The familiar linear trope of nationalism dictates the depiction of the Korean experience in terms of oppression and resistance with the goal of liberating Korea. The story’s narrative strategy juxtaposes the two conjoined paths taken by Ch’angyun and his son, Chŏngsu: Ch’angyun’s continuous displacement and Chŏngsu’s education and participation in the noncommunist resistance. When Koreans in Ch’angyun’s village fail to identify the killer of the deceased Chinese man, Chinese officials levy fines on the whole village. Beleaguered by heightened tensions and penalties and motivated by rumors of a better life elsewhere, Koreans begin to migrate. Pukkando describes the migration in this way: “One family, two families, they abandon their Pibongch’on village without hesitation to leave for a place where they can live well. This is a kind of wind. It is a blustery wind. Driven by that wind, people in Pibongch’on, family by family, go forward with ragged hope.”

Some leave for cities, new mining towns, or Russia. Others leave to farm in mountainous areas in northern Manchuria. During the relocations, Ch’angyun’s family subsists by running a noodle shop in a city, making bricks, returning to farming, and then running a noodle shop again. The courageous resistance of Koreans is intertwined with this narrative of displacement. Uprooted from their land and family, Ch’angyun’s brother even more than Ch’angyun vainly struggles to make a living in the city. He eventually joins the independence army to liberate Korea and finally dies in battle. Unlike Ch’angyun’s brother, Ch’angyun’s son obtains an education and earns a stable living as a teacher, but he also partakes in the anti-Japanese liberation movement.

zh: 民族时间与资本主义时间
en: National and Capitalist Time

zh: 在《北间岛》中，民族时间把朝鲜人的流离封装为无国之民的重复经验。民族时间把他们的经验抽象为所有朝鲜人——无论在朝鲜、间岛还是满洲其他地方——共有的单一空间意识。除中国政府的角色外，朝鲜人在满洲内部的流离被表象为与他们此前从朝鲜的流离无从区分。每一个流离时刻都由一串事件标记：朝鲜人遭地主与官员勒索，累积债务，失去抵押的土地，逃往新地方。民族时间同质化所有流离朝鲜人的社会经验。以民族叙事呈现流离经历，排挤了对自身劳动及其产品享有权利的地方社会意识——Ch'angyun与邻人此前曾接合出的那种意识——也排挤了与中国人民结成统一战线的全球意识。
en: In Pukkando, national time encapsulates the displacement of Koreans as a repetitive experience of a people without a nation. National time abstracts their experience into a single spatial consciousness for all Koreans, whether in Korea, Kando, or other parts of Manchuria. Except for the role of the Chinese government, Koreans’ displacement within Manchuria is represented as indistinguishable from their prior displacement from Korea. Each moment of displacement is marked by a chain of events: Koreans are subject to extortion by landlords and officials, they accumulate debt, they lose their mortgaged land, and they flee to a new place. National time homogenizes the social experience of all displaced Koreans. The national representation of displacement dislodges both a local social consciousness of the rights to one’s own labor and its products—the one that Ch’angyun and his neighbors had articulated earlier and a global consciousness about the united front with the Chinese people.

zh: 这种民族时间的叙述也呈现了民族的危机，暗示间岛朝鲜人脱离朝鲜民族主义。对照父子两代人路径的叙事策略——忠于土地的农民Ch'angyun与作为教师兼活动家的儿子——有使耕作与启蒙分离的危险，而这两者曾由Ch'angyun的祖父统一起来。这种统一曾作为一种新朝鲜民族主义的象征，被想象在间岛——贫困而未受教育的农民的新边疆——实现。社会生活与朝鲜民族辩证统一所受的威胁，进一步被以下事实强化：Ch'angyun成功说服儿子投靠日本领事馆警察署。Ch'angyun这一不忠之举，出于他的焦虑：参加独立运动会危及儿子的教育与未来生计。除朝鲜与满洲从日本解放前夕的几个月——其间他因策划反日活动再次入狱——之外，尽管旧日同志催促他加入游击斗争，他始终远离政治。Ch'angyun的早死，部分归因于他对影响儿子向日本权力投降这一决定的内疚。Ch'angyun之死或许正是垂死的朝鲜民族与在满朝鲜人枯萎的民族主义的症状。
en: This narration of national time also presents the crisis of the nation, insinuating the departure of the Koreans of Kando from Korean nationalism. The narrative strategy of contrasting the passages of father and son— Ch’angyun as the devoted farmer and his son as a schoolteacher and activist—risks the separation of farming and enlightenment, which Ch’angyun’s grandfather had unified. This unity worked as a symbol of a new Korean nationalism that was imagined to be realized in Kando, a new frontier for impoverished and uneducated peasants. The threat to the dialectical unity of social life and the Korean nation is further accentuated by the fact that Ch’angyun successfully persuades his son to defect to a Japanese consulate police station. This unfaithful act of Ch’angyun was forced by his anxiety that participation in the independence movement would jeopardize his son’s education and future livelihood. Except for several months just before the liberation of Korea and Manchuria from Japan, during which time he would again be imprisoned for planning anti-Japanese activities, he stays away from politics despite the urging of his former comrades to join the guerrilla struggle. Ch’angyun’s premature death is in part attributed to his guilt over influencing his son’s decision to surrender to Japanese power. Ch’angyun’s death is perhaps symptomatic of the dying Korean nation and withering nationalism of Koreans in Manchuria.

zh: 超历史的民族时间充当资本主义历时时间的容器。民族时间把朝鲜人的资本主义经验自然化为民族压迫的副产品。Ch'angyun村里朝鲜人的流离被表象为中国民族主义与日本帝国主义加剧的结果。这使民族时间与资本主义时间之间的关键关系变得不透明。当Ch'angyun一家与旧邻从日本一家拓殖会社获得贷款购买农田时，叙事并未阐发这些朝日经济纽带对资本主义扩张的意涵。其他商品化症状，如城市的工资劳动、日工与行商，只被陈述而未探究其资本主义意义。《北间岛》中对共产主义领导的政治只字不提，或许是该书线性民族主义叙事对资本主义更大沉默的又一标志。
en: Transhistorical national time serves as a container for the diachronic time of capitalism. National time naturalizes the capitalist experiences of Koreans as a byproduct of national oppression. The displacement of Koreans in Ch’angyun’s village is represented as the effect of mounting Chinese nationalism and Japanese imperialism. This makes the crucial relationship between national and capitalist time opaque. When Ch’angyun’s family and former neighbors receive loans from a Japanese development company to purchase farmland, the narrative does not elaborate the implications for capitalist expansion of these economic ties between Koreans and Japanese. Other symptoms of commodification, such as wage and day labor and peddling in cities, are stated without exploring their capitalist significance. The absence of any reference to communist-led politics in Pukkando is perhaps another sign of a larger silence about capitalism in the linear nationalist narratives of the book.

zh: 朝鲜人的双重位置必须被理解为土地与劳动力商品化的共同悖论效应——朝鲜人、中国民族主义、日本帝国主义三方都促成了这一效应。朝鲜移民与日本权力是共享资本主义之梦的同床者。日本权力嵌入了被殖民朝鲜人保住社会生活与土地所有权之梦。朝鲜人的交换价值包括他们认为可以从与日本权力的关系中得到的好处。此外，中国民族主义与日本殖民主义也是同床者，共享迅速把满洲商业化的梦想。当中国政府禁止未入籍朝鲜人拥有财产、从而占有其土地时，中国民族主义与资本主义扩张不可分离。事实上，中国东北政府在满洲的土地与农业商业上投入重金。尽管一再呼吁驱逐未入籍朝鲜人，它同时却从这一政策退却，甚至正式允许朝鲜人作为农业劳动者与短期佃农留下。与中国压迫相配合，日本的贷款使朝鲜农民得以从间岛迁往南满与北满。他们把荒地变为有利可图的农田，加快了商品化的步伐。朝鲜人被逐离土地的过程，就是他们失去对生产资料控制的过程。当他们因中国压迫或无力偿还日本组织贷款而被强行逐离土地时，他们失去了在土地与灌溉设施等基础设施上投入劳动所积累的成果。被夺走的土地，或他们相对于中国（及日本）同行所付的高额地租与地价，都是朝鲜人在不同时间地点的交换关系中所受剥削的指标。要更充分理解中日围绕朝鲜人国籍与土地所有权的争端，必须分析资本积累的动力。
en: The dual position of Koreans must be understood as a joint paradoxical effect of the commodification of land and labor, an effect to which all three parties—Koreans, Chinese nationalism, and Japanese imperialism— contributed. Korean migrants and Japanese power are bedfellows who share a capitalist dream. Japanese power has embedded in the dream of the colonized Koreans to secure social life and landownership. The exchange value of Koreans includes their perceived benefits in relation to Japanese power. Moreover, Chinese nationalism and Japanese colonialism are also bedfellows, sharing the dream of swiftly commercializing Manchuria. When the Chinese government banned unnaturalized Koreans from owning property and thus appropriated their land, Chinese nationalism was inseparable from capitalist expansion. In fact, the Chinese Northeast government invested heavily in land and agricultural commerce in Manchuria. Though repeatedly calling for the eviction of unnaturalized Koreans, it simultaneously retreated from this policy and even officially allowed Koreans to remain as agricultural laborers and short-term tenants. In tandem with Chinese oppression, the loans from the Japanese enabled Korean peasants to migrate from Kando to South and North Manchuria. Their transformation of wasteland into lucrative farmland hastened the pace of commodification. Displacement of Koreans from their land is the process whereby they lost control over their means of production. When they are forcibly removed from their land by Chinese oppression or the failure to repay the loans from Japanese organizations, they lost the products of the labor that they had applied to the land and infrastructure such as irrigation systems. The land taken away from Koreans or the high rents and land prices they had to pay in comparison with what their Chinese (and Japanese) counterparts paid are indicators of the exploitation that Koreans experienced in exchange relations at different times and places. An analysis of the dynamics of capital accumulation is necessary for a fuller understanding of the disputes between China and Japan over the citizenship and landownership of Koreans.

zh: 流离呈现了资本主义身体性的另一面。流离并非游牧移动本身，而是一种有明确驱动力且会产生具体后果的移动形式。民族时间把资本主义时间自然化，后者随即把社会经验普遍化，同时又把一个流离时刻与另一个区分开来。朝鲜人的身体移动是商品化渗透扩散的过程。它是一种清除生产与市场交换障碍的“社会新陈代谢”。每一次迁移旅程都是土地与劳动的价值被创造与占有的实例。流离的重复是资本积累的实例，其中土地与劳动连同其在市场上的交换价值一起被商品化。朝鲜人的交换价值不仅因日中权力本身的对抗而上升，它也由其劳动力在市场上的不平等交换所决定。
en: Displacement presents a different side of capitalist corporeality. Displacement is not nomadic movement per se but rather a form of movement that has definite forces and effects. National time naturalizes capitalist time, which then universalizes the social experience even as it concurrently distinguishes one moment of displacement from another. The corporeal movement of Koreans is a process of osmotic diffusion of commodification. It is a form of “social metabolism” that removes barriers to production and market exchange. Each migration journey is an instance in which the value of land and labor is created and appropriated. The repetition of displacement is an instance of capital accumulation in which land and labor are commodified along with their exchange value in the market. The exchange value of Koreans not only increased in response to the rivalry of the Japanese and Chinese powers per se. It was also determined by the unequal exchange of their labor power in the market.

zh: 资本主义时间让朝鲜人在参加解放朝鲜的民族主义运动之外，还能展开一种新的日常政治。他们的日常政治还应在作为劳动者与地主和资本讨价还价的能力中、在其具体的生产与交换关系中加以评估。即使迁移之后，朝鲜人在定居一地之前至少还在满洲内部移动了三四次。朝鲜人的多次迁移获得双重含义。迁移、耕作、被逐、再迁移的循环把日本与中国权力带到满洲的边缘地区，因为国家权力追逐朝鲜人，以主张对其定居地区的主权与所有权。它也体现了他们作为流离移民劳动者的主体性：他们希望调和自己的朝鲜民族身份（规避日中双方压力）与对劳动的主权（对投入劳动的土地的事实所有权）。朝鲜人的多次迁移证明了他们与日中双方的谈判能力，这种能力源于朝鲜人的水稻种植技术。
en: Capitalist time authorized a new everyday politics for Koreans beyond their participation in the nationalist movement to liberate Korea. Their everyday politics is also to be assessed in their bargaining power as labor vis-à-vis landlords/capital and in their concrete relations of production and exchange. Even after Koreans migrated, they moved at least three or four times within Manchuria before they settled in one place. The multiple migrations of Koreans acquired a double meaning. The cycle of migration, cultivation, eviction, and remigration carried Japanese and Chinese power to peripheral areas in Manchuria, as the state powers chased after Koreans to claim sovereignty and ownership over the areas they had settled. It also embodied their subjectivities as displaced migrant laborers who desired to harmonize their Korean national identities (the evasion of both Japanese and Chinese pressure) and sovereignty over their labor (de facto ownership of the land to which they applied their labor). The multiple migrations of Koreans attest to their negotiating power with both the Japanese and Chinese, which was derived from the rice-farming skills of Koreans.

zh: 朝鲜人在满洲的社会经验超出了此前对民族的空间认同，也超出了流离与民族主义政治的线性时间性。他们在国籍与土地所有权上的变异实践，展示了其主体性的多重场所与时间性。日中（清与民国时期的中国东北政府）之间的领土竞争围绕朝鲜人的身份与制度权利问题展开。然而无论日本还是中国，都未能控制朝鲜人迁移、耕作与市场交换的方向，更谈不上总体化其身份。无论是否入籍为中国国民，无论在满洲国时期之前还是期间，朝鲜人持续持有双重国籍。即使入籍为中国国民，其国籍也采取各种文化的、法律的、共同体的和/或以户为基础的形式。此外，入籍朝鲜人继续被识别为朝鲜人/日本人。当大多数朝鲜人仍未入籍、缺乏有保障的土地所有权且流动不居时，他们被视为朝鲜总督府与日本帝国（包括满洲国）的臣民。他们的土地所有权结合了私有、长期租佃、共同体所有与各种贷款。作为公民与劳动者的人的社会形态，在不同历史情势中相互构成。
en: Koreans’ social experience in Manchuria exceeded a prior spatial identification with their nation, as well as a linear temporality of displacement and nationalist politics. Their aberrant practices of nationality and landownership demonstrate the multiple places and temporalities of their subjectivities. Territorial rivalry between Japan and China (the Northeast Chinese government during the Qing and Republican periods) revolved around issues of the identities and institutional rights of Koreans. Neither Japan nor China, however, succeeded in controlling the direction of Korean migration, farming, and market exchanges, let alone totalizing their identities. Whether naturalized as Chinese nationals and whether before or during the Manchukuo period, Koreans continued to hold dual nationality. Even when they became naturalized as Chinese, their nationality took various cultural, legal, collective, and/or household-based forms. Moreover, naturalized Koreans continued to be identified as Koreans/Japanese. When the majority of Koreans remained unnaturalized, lacked secure rights to ownership of land, and were mobile, they were considered subjects of the Government General of Korea and the Japanese empire (including Manchukuo). Their landownership combined private ownership, long-term leasing, communal landownership, and various loans. The social formations of people as citizens and laborers are mutually constituted at different historical junctures.

zh: 民族时间与资本主义时间规定不同种类的全球意识与行动。前者把全球性设想为绑定于不同领土、在边界争端中激烈对抗的不同民族共同体的集合。民族时间抹除地方经验。资本主义时间则通过把地方经验置于全球过程之中来引导全球意识。由于社会关系在原则上与现实中都受资本动力支配，社会关系超出民族边界，使全球意识对于各地人民的解放不仅可能而且必要。在日本帝国中，朝鲜、满洲、台湾与日本的农民通过生产与再生产上的相互依赖而联结。间岛每个朝鲜农民的农业生产受世界市场作物需求的调节，而再生产日益依赖朝鲜与日本的工人——他们生产在满朝鲜人消费的商品。满洲劳动者生产的农产品出口，改变了朝鲜与日本的生产与交换关系。
en: National and capitalist times prescribe different kinds of global consciousness and actions. The former conceives globality as an amalgamation of different national communities bound to different territories and potently antagonistic in the case of border disputes. National time obliterates local experience. Capitalist time directs global consciousness by placing local experience in a global process. Because social relations are governed by capital dynamics, in principle and reality, social relations exceed national boundaries, making a global consciousness not just possible but necessary for the liberation of people in each locality. In the Japanese empire, peasants in Korea, Manchuria, Taiwan, and Japan were linked through their reliance on each other for production and reproduction. Agricultural production by each Korean peasant in Kando was regulated by the demand for crops in the world market, and reproduction increasingly depended on workers in Korea and Japan who produced the goods consumed by Koreans in Manchuria. The export of agricultural products produced by laborers in Manchuria transformed the relations of production and exchange in Korea and Japan.

zh: 尽管各地社会关系因其独特政治与文化而带有地方区别，它们仍通过交换链条与其他地方的社会关系整合。全球意识因此伴随地方分化与全球整合的矛盾过程而推进。能够把人民从资本主义压迫中解放出来的全球运动，不是单一统一实体，而是多重具体斗争，每一斗争都嵌入地方经验与全球语境的独特相互联系之中。这种新共同体的创造要求辩证地化解全球意识与地方意识之间的关系——以领土为界的民族主义则把两者描绘为彼此无法调和的对立面。满洲的地方斗争必须接合朝鲜人经验的多重时间性，以及他们与中国人、日本人的关系。
en: While they bear a local distinction by virtue of their unique politics and culture, social relations in each locality are integrated with those of other localities through the chain of exchange. Global consciousness thus proceeds with the contradictory processes of local differentiations and global integration. A global movement capable of liberating people from capitalist oppression is not a single unified entity but a multiplicity of concrete struggles, each of which is embedded in the distinctive interconnections of local experience and the global context. The creation of this new community requires a dialectical resolution of the relationship between global and local consciousness, which territory-bound nationalism represents as the irreconcilable other. Local struggles in Manchuria must articulate the multiple temporalities of Koreans’ experiences, as well as their relations with Chinese and Japanese.

zh: 这里讨论的《北间岛》三个情节表明，朝鲜人源于被殖民者与殖民者双重位置的空间与时间经验，要求仔细分析交织的民族与资本主义动力。下一节把民族国家体系（及民族主义）概念化为帝国领土与资本主义扩张的单位。它还阐发领土扩张与资本主义扩张之间的辩证统一与张力。但让我先考察这一命题：朝鲜移民是日本帝国构建的跨国模式。
en: The three episodes of Pukkando discussed here demonstrate that the spatial and temporal experiences of Koreans, arising from their double position as the colonized and the colonizer, demand careful analysis of the entangled national and capitalist dynamics. The next section conceptualizes the nation-state system (and nationalism) as the unit of territorial and capitalist expansion of the empire. It also elaborates the dialectical unity and tension between territorial and capitalist expansion. But let me first examine the proposition that Korean migration was a transnational mode of Japanese empire building.

zh: 渗透政治
en: the politics of osmosis

zh: 日本帝国的渗透扩张体现在日本殖民朝鲜、然后把朝鲜与满洲配对以进行下一轮对华渗透的方式中。迁往满洲的朝鲜移民——主要是农民——充当了日本权力从朝鲜向满洲渗透扩散的“分子”。日本把朝鲜移民想象为流体般的能动者，能够穿过朝鲜边界的膜进入满洲——那里溶剂浓度（即对日本干预的抵抗）更高。以此方式，日本希望朝鲜人在满洲的迁移与定居能中和中国的抵抗，使日本权力的逐步扩散成为可能。绝大多数朝鲜移民是想逃离贫困与债务的无地农民。在满洲的一部分——间岛，自1900年代以来朝鲜人占总人口的三分之二以上。日本对间岛朝鲜人的统治，在1932年满洲国建立之前就被等同于殖民。
en: The osmotic expansion of the Japanese empire is demonstrated in the way Japan colonized Korea and then paired Korea and Manchuria for the next round of infiltration into China. Korean migrants to Manchuria, mainly peasants, served as “molecules” in the osmotic diffusion of Japan’s power from Korea to Manchuria. Japan imagined Korean migrants as if they were fluid agents that could pass through the membrane of Korea’s borders into Manchuria, where the solvent concentration (or resistance to Japan’s intervention) was higher. In this way, Japan hoped that the migration and settlement of Koreans in Manchuria would neutralize Chinese resistance, making possible a gradual diffusion of Japan’s power. The vast majority of the Korean migrants were landless peasants who wanted to escape poverty and debt. In one part of Manchuria, Kando, Koreans had comprised more than two-thirds of the total population since the 1900s. Japan’s rule over Koreans in Kando was equated with colonization even before the establishment of Manchukuo in 1932.

zh: 中国的困境在于：它既不能驱逐朝鲜移民，也不能忽视他们——尽管到1931年他们占满洲总人口的比例还不到 5%。作为与朝鲜（Chosŏn）围绕间岛领土争端的临时解决，清政府于19世纪末授予朝鲜人在间岛耕作与居住的习惯权利。在此之前，满洲一直是人口稀少的腹地，作为清朝皇帝的发祥地与猎场而保留。由于中国人向满洲的迁移缓慢，清政府希望朝鲜定居者能构成对俄国帝国主义威胁的缓冲。即使民国时期（1912–31）华北农民迁移迅速扩大，张作霖领导的中国东北政府仍在旨在阻止朝鲜移民的政策与旨在利用移民作为稻农的政策之间摇摆。在徒劳地试图把朝鲜人逐出满洲的同时，政府试图主张对他们的主权，以挫败日本的殖民野心。中日对抗变成了对朝鲜人的争夺。
en: The predicament for China was that it could neither evict Korean migrants nor ignore them, although they constituted at best less than 5 percent of the total population of Manchuria by 1931. As a temporary resolution of territorial disputes with Korea (Chosŏn) over Kando, the Qing government granted Koreans customary rights to farming and residence in Kando in the late nineteenth century. Before that time, Manchuria had been a sparsely populated hinterland preserved as the birthplace and hunting grounds of the Qing emperors. As the migration of Chinese to Manchuria was slow, the Qing government hoped that the Korean settlers would create a buffer from the threat of Russian imperialism. Even when the migration of peasants from North China rapidly expanded during the Republican period (1912–31), the Northeast Chinese government, led by Zhang Zuolin, vacillated between policies intended to prevent Korean migration and policies intended to utilize the migrants as rice growers. While vainly trying to evict Koreans from Manchuria, the government attempted to assert its sovereignty over them in order to thwart Japanese colonial ambitions. The confrontation between China and Japan became a competition over Koreans.

zh: 中国与朝鲜移民在满洲的主要路线不同。港口与铁路的发展加速了来自中国本部的移民。中国农民一般乘船或铁路从华北迁往南满，尤其经由1907年由英国人建成的北京—奉天（沈阳，南满奉天省省会）铁路线。从南满，他们乘南满铁路或中东铁路向东、向北扩散。相反，在满朝鲜移民从东北向西南与北方移动。自19世纪末起，他们最初集中于东满的间岛地区，不仅因为间岛被视为朝鲜领土，也因为图们江边界易于跨越。朝鲜人在南满的定居主要始于20世纪初，他们从间岛或朝鲜迁来，跨越流经南满与朝鲜之间的鸭绿江。朝鲜人从奉天省称为东边道（Tongbyŏndo）的山区边界地带迁往北满与东满。间岛朝鲜人也迁往吉林与黑龙江省，以逃避自然灾害与日本对流亡朝鲜独立运动的镇压。
en: The main routes of Chinese and Korean migration in Manchuria were different. The development of ports and railways expedited migration from China proper. Chinese peasants in general moved from Northern China to southern Manchuria by ship or railway, especially via the railway line between Beijing and Mukden (Shenyang, the capital of Fengtian Province in South Manchuria), which had been completed by the British in 1907. From South Manchuria, they spread east and north by taking the South Manchuria Railway or the Eastern Chinese Railway. In contrast, Korean migrants in Manchuria moved from the northeast to the southwest and north. From the late nineteenth century on, they initially concentrated in the Kando region in East Manchuria, not only because Kando was regarded as Korean territory but also because it was easy to cross the border at the Tuman River. Korean settlement in South Manchuria mainly began in the early twentieth century, as Koreans migrated from Kando or Korea, crossing the Apnok River, which ran between South Manchuria and Korea. Koreans moved from the mountainous border region of Fengtian Province, called Tongbyŏndo, to North and East Manchuria. Koreans in Kando also migrated to Jilin and Heilongjiang Provinces, fleeing from natural disasters and the Japanese suppression of exiled Korean independence movements.

zh: 朝鲜移民是日本帝国主义研究中一个重要却被忽视的主题。

文献以正式与非正式形式刻画日本殖民。正式殖民指以“血与铁”吞并朝鲜或台湾等殖民地。日本在每个殖民地领土内持有排他主权，要求被殖民者取得日本护照或其他身份证明、承担日本兵役、提供捐献与劳役，并接受制度性同化与监视。这里日本对被殖民人民的主权是领土性与制度性的。非正式殖民指不平等条约带来的政治与经济干预。典型个案是1895至1937年日本对中国本部的渗透。开启日本此后半个世纪支配地位的1895年《马关条约》，赋予日本进入通商口岸、设厂、贸易以及在华居住旅行的权利。1937年日本侵华被视为这种非正式统治的终结。
en: Korean migration is an important yet neglected theme in the study of Japanese imperialism.

The literature characterizes Japanese colonization in terms of formal and informal forms. Formal colonization refers to the annexation of a colony such as Korea or Taiwan by means of “blood and iron.” Japan held exclusive sovereignty within the territory of each colony, requiring the colonized to obtain a Japanese passport or other identification, be liable for Japanese military conscription, provide donations and labor, and be subject to institutional assimilation and surveillance. Here Japan’s sovereignty over its colonized peoples was territorial and institutional. Informal colonization denotes political and economic interventions brought about by unequal treaties. A paradigmatic case is the Japanese penetration into China proper from 1895 to 1937. Inaugurating Japanese dominance for the next half century, the Shimonoseki Treaty of 1895 provided Japan with the rights to access trading ports, build factories, engage in trade, and live and travel in the country. Japan’s invasion of China in 1937 is considered to be the end of this informal rule.

zh: 领土殖民与非正式殖民的二元模式遮蔽了另一种延伸统治的形式——跨国领土渗透——其中朝鲜移民构成日本帝国形成的跨国机制。

在渗透过程中，日本的主权并不驻留于殖民地内的国家机构，也不限于日本臣民的治外法权、以及保护宗主国与满洲之间资本、商品与资源的流通。渗透过程揭示了一种跨国“身体政治”，朝鲜移民借此把日本权力从朝鲜携带过边界进入满洲。日本身体政治的另一个例子，是它主张满洲、西藏与蒙古的主权不在中国国家而在这些地区的王公手中。日本首相1927年声称：“过去中国虽谈五族共和，但西藏、新疆、蒙古与满洲始终保留为特殊地区，王公被允许行使其习惯职能。因此实际上这些地区的主权掌握在王公手中……只要那里的王公维持其原有行政，主权权利显然在他们手中。”在这一规定中，承载这些地区主权的是王公的身体，而非国家机构。
在这种身体政治中，日本在满洲的权力行使表明，主权未必对应于国家对该地区的权力。
en: The binary mode of territorial and informal colonization obscures another form of extending rule—transnational territorial osmosis—in which Korean migrants constituted a transnational mechanism in the formation of the Japanese empire.

In the osmotic process, Japan’s sovereignty did not reside in state institutions within a colony. Nor was it confined to the extraterritoriality of Japan’s subjects and to protecting the circulation of capital, goods, and resources between metropole and Manchuria. The osmotic process reveals a transnational “body politics” through which Korean migrants carried Japan’s power across the border from Korea to Manchuria. Another example of Japanese body politics is its assertion that sovereignty in Manchuria, Tibet, and Mongolia rested not with the Chinese state but with the princes of these regions. The prime minister of Japan stated in 1927 that “in the past although China speaks of the Republic of Five Races, yet Tibet, Sinkiang, Mongolia, and Manchuria have always remained special areas and the princes are permitted to discharge their customary functions. Therefore in reality the sovereign power over these resided with the princes. . . . So long as the princes there maintain their former administrations, the sovereign rights are clearly in their hands.” In this stipulation, the bodies of princes, not state institutions, harbor sovereign power in these regions.
In this corporeal politics, Japan’s exercise of power in Manchuria shows that sovereignty did not necessarily correspond to state power over the region.
